alignments.note: Article before the name Παῦλος; the ASV writes no determiner for it (rule 23).
δέ → But.
Name aligned on its own token (rule 26).
ἔφη → said.
πρός → unto; the English preposition governing the phrase realizes the Greek preposition (rule 36).
Accusative pronoun object of πρός.
Circumstantial participle recast as a finite clause; the supplied subject They and the auxiliary have are helpers under rules 7 and 9, and rule 17 heads on the lexical verb beaten.

ἡμᾶς → us, the expressed object of beaten. The second us before into prison is a supplied object of ἔβαλαν and rides with that verb under rules 7 and 74, as every other supplied object in this chapter does (16.14, 16.15, 16.23, 16.39). Reading it as a discontinuous second realization of this token under rule 15 remains defensible.
δημοσίᾳ → publicly.
Attributive adjective → uncondemned.
ἀνθρώπους → men; anarthrous noun with no determiner supplied.
Participle rendered as a finite relative clause; the relativizer that is its helper under rules 7 and 31, and are glosses ὑπάρχοντας itself, so it takes the head.
Predicate of the relative clause, split from the participle under rule 2 though the English reorders it (rule 15).

The supplied juncture and introduces this finite verb after the participial clause of s007 and is its helper, never added (rule 88); have is the auxiliary. The supplied object pronoun us is a rule 7 helper on the verb that requires it in English, as rule 74 has it and as ἔβαλον → they cast them does at 16.23. Rule 17 heads on cast.
εἰς → into.
φυλακήν → prison, anarthrous with no determiner written.
Expressed καί → and.
νῦν → now.

Interrogative do and the subject they are inflection-licensed helpers under rule 9; the preverb ἐκ- is realized by out inside the verb's own unit, discontinuously, and rule 106 heads on the verb word cast.
Object of ἐκβάλλουσιν.
λάθρᾳ → privily, reordered to the end of the clause (rule 15).
Plain negative → nay; no second negative word stands, so rules 41 and 59 do not arise.
γάρ → verily; the ASV writes a word for the particle, so it is aligned rather than emptied (rule 70's English-side test).
ἀλλά → but.
Participle recast as the first member of the imperative clause; only come answers to it, the auxiliary let them belonging to the third-person imperative s028 under rules 9 and 73.
Intensive αὐτοί → themselves.
Object of ἐξαγαγέτωσαν.

Third-person imperative: the periphrastic let them is its own auxiliary, kept discontinuously as rule 73 keeps let with its imperative, and the juncture and introduces this finite verb under rule 88; the preverb ἐξ- is realized by out inside the unit (rule 106) and rule 17 heads on bring. Reading let them as a helper on the nearer verb come remains defensible, but the imperative is what licenses it.

review_notes: Corrected: t019 us now rides with ἔβαλαν as a rule 7 helper on the verb that requires an object in English (rule 74), and s008 ἡμᾶς keeps only t009. This aligns the verse with 16.23's ἔβαλον → they cast them, the identical construction.
Reading t019 as a discontinuous second realization of ἡμᾶς under rule 15, or as added under rule 103, remains defensible and is named in the units' notes.
Every source and target id is partitioned exactly once; only s001 is unrepresented.
The two supplied junctures (t016, t037) stay on the finite verbs they introduce per rule 88, since each follows a Greek participle recast as a coordinate clause.
